questions.question: What does a finite series represent?
options: The sum of finitely many terms of a sequence.
A sequence with infinitely many partial sums only.
A function with no domain.
A proof that a sequence is unbounded.

questions.question: In the notation $S_n = \sum_{i = 1}^n a_i$, what is being summed?
options: Only the first and last terms $a_1$ and $a_n$.
The terms $a_i$ for integer indices $1\leq i\leq n$.
All real numbers between $1$ and $n$.
Only the index values $i$ without the terms $a_i$.

questions.question: What is $\displaystyle \sum_{i = 1}^5 i$?
What is $\displaystyle \sum_{i = 1}^3 2^i$?
What initial value is used in the recursive definition of a finite series?
Why do finite series not involve convergence issues?
options: Every term must be zero.
Only finitely many terms are added.
The index set is always unbounded.
The sum is always equal to $1$.

questions.question: If $S_2 = 5$ and $a_3 = 4$, what is $S_3$ using the recursive formula?
For $a_1 = 2$, $a_2 = -1$, and $a_3 = 5$, what is $\displaystyle \sum_{i = 1}^3 a_i$?
Which statement correctly describes the finite sequence used in a finite series?
options: The terms $a_i$ must form an infinite sequence before the sum is defined.
The terms $a_i$ must be natural numbers only.
The terms $a_i$ must come from a finite sequence of real numbers.
The terms $a_i$ are not assigned to indices.

questions.question: The recursion $S_n=S_{n-1}+a_n$ needs a starting value. Why does this force $\sum_{i=1}^{0}a_i=0$?
options: It is equal to $a_1$.
It is the base case $S_0 = 0$.
It is undefined because finite series never allow $n = 0$.
It is equal to $1$.

questions.question: Using the recursive definition, if $a_i = i$ then what is $S_4$?
A student worries that $\displaystyle \sum_{i = 1}^3 a_i$ might diverge. Which response is correct?
options: It diverges unless every $a_i$ is positive.
It converges only if $a_3 = 0$.
It is a finite series, so convergence issues do not arise.
It is not a sum because the upper limit is finite.

questions.question: What is the difference between a finite series and an infinite series?
options: A finite series adds only finitely many terms.
A finite series has no terms.
A finite series always diverges.
A finite series is indexed by all real numbers.

questions.question: What does the recursive relation $S_n=S_{n-1}+a_n$ express?
options: The next partial sum is obtained by adding the next term.
The next partial sum is obtained by multiplying by $n$.
The sum is always $0$.
The terms are not indexed.

questions.question: Why do finite series avoid convergence issues?
options: Every finite series has infinitely many terms.
Every term must be positive.
The sum is never a number.
Only finitely many terms are added.

questions.question: What is $\sum_{i=1}^{4}2$?
What is $\sum_{i=1}^{3} i^2$?
What is the base case value $S_0$ in the recursive definition?
Why is every finite series well-defined once the terms are real numbers?
options: Because it requires an infinite limiting process.
Because it uses only finitely many ordinary additions.
Because it ignores the terms $a_i$.
Because the upper index must be $+\infty$.
